ops.body:
Regex patterns shared between `cc_transcript/filterspec.py` and the Rust backend (protocol markers, filterspec/mining/score groups) are authored once, in Python, in a **dialect-hardened subset** that Python `re` and the Rust `regex` crate interpret identically. The generated constants in `rust/src/generated/` and the JSON spec contract both transport these pattern strings verbatim, so every pattern must stay inside the subset.

## The hardening rules

- **`\A\s*` start anchoring** (not `^`): banners must match only at content start so a mid-text mention is never treated as a banner; `\A` has identical semantics in both engines regardless of multiline flags.
- **`(?-i:[Ii])` ASCII pinning** for case-insensitive letters that must not Unicode-fold (e.g. the "i" in `[Role Rem(?-i:[Ii])nder` and the "i" in `[Request (?-i:[Ii])nterrupted by user`): under `(?i)`, Python and Rust disagree on dotted/dotless-I folding (İ/ı, U+0130/U+0131). Pinning the class to ASCII `[Ii]` keeps both engines byte-identical.
- **Explicit follower classes instead of `\b`** (e.g. `(?:[\s:\]]|$)`): word-boundary semantics diverge across combining marks (U+0301 etc.) between the engines; an explicit class is portable.
- **No lookaround, no backreferences**: the Rust `regex` crate rejects them (`mining/spec.py` `UNPORTABLE_RE` gates this for mining specs).
- **Flags travel out-of-band**: Python composes flag-free alternations via `filterspec.group_pattern` and applies `re.IGNORECASE` at compile; Rust applies `(?i)` at its compile sites. Pattern strings themselves stay flag-free.
- **`\s` C0-separator divergence is accepted, not worked around**: Python `\s` matches the C0 information separators U+001C–U+001F, Rust `\s` does not. For the leading `\s*` in banner patterns this is a known, theoretical-only divergence that never occurs in real transcripts — do not contort the pattern to close it.

## The gates that enforce this

- `PORTABLE_GROUP_NAMES` (`cc_transcript/filterspec.py`) — the explicit allowlist of group names proven to match identically under the Rust regex crate; a renamed or new group must be added deliberately or specs silently fall back to the Python path.
- `tests/test_literals_parity.py` — embedded Rust constants == Python source, plus generator freshness.
- The `rust/src/protocol.rs` unit tests (`agent_injection_rejects_prose_and_mid_text_mentions`, `interrupt_marker_is_head_anchored_and_case_folded`, the U+0301 combining-mark and U+0130/U+0131 dotted/dotless-I cases) — the executable half of this rationale.
- The differential corpus suites (`tests/test_filter_parity.py`, `test_mining_parity.py`) — Python is the oracle.

When editing any shared pattern: stay inside the subset above, keep the group name portable-listed, regenerate `rust/src/generated/` via `scripts/build_rust_literals.py`, and land Python + Rust + re-pin in one commit (AGENTS.md "Rust parity is atomic").
